description: Calculate the annualized refrigerant leak rate at each addition and compare it with the EPA leak-repair threshold for the appliance type. Use this tested BusCalc worksheet when the task matches its inputs and scope. Returns named results, units, formula, assumptions, method version, reference-value notes (official figure or your figure, with source and effective date), a check link and a source-page URL. Official reference values are prefilled when omitted; supply every other figure from the user's records. Percent fields take percent numbers. No figures are looked up; no private projects or purchases are accessed. Put tool fields inside inputs. Supply units or modelVersion only when listed in inputSchema. Follow its required fields and exact choices. Do not pass the REST calculator field inside MCP arguments.

added.description: Refrigerant added at this service (lb). Pounds added to return the appliance to a full charge, from the service record. Used only when mode is single; ignored otherwise.

appliance.description: Appliance type. Use matching records or an explicitly identified assumption for appliance type. Unknown is not the same as zero. Options: commercial = Commercial refrigeration; ipr = Industrial process refrigeration; comfort = Comfort cooling; other = Refrigerated transport or other appliance.

coverage.description: Full charge at which the leak-repair rule applies (lb). Use matching records or an explicitly identified assumption for full charge at which the leak-repair rule applies. Unknown is not the same as zero. Official reference value 15 lb from 40 CFR 84.106 applicability (EPA AIM Act ER&R rule), effective 2026-01-01. Omit to use it; enter your own figure to override. The result notes say which was used.

days.description: Days since the previous addition (days). Days from the last day refrigerant was added; more than 365 is capped at 365. Used only when mode is single; ignored otherwise.

events.description: Service log of additions. Use matching records or an explicitly identified assumption for service log of additions. Unknown is not the same as zero. Used only when mode is log; ignored otherwise.

added.description: Refrigerant added (lb). Use matching records or an explicitly identified assumption for refrigerant added. Unknown is not the same as zero.

day.description: Day number of this addition (day). Use matching records or an explicitly identified assumption for day number of this addition. Unknown is not the same as zero.

fullCharge.description: Appliance full charge (lb). The full charge recorded for the appliance (nameplate, manufacturer data or your documented full-charge determination).

mode.description: Calculation mode. Use matching records or an explicitly identified assumption for calculation mode. Unknown is not the same as zero. Options: single = One refrigerant addition; log = Service log of additions.

repairDays.description: Days to identify and repair leaks after the addition (days). Use matching records or an explicitly identified assumption for days to identify and repair leaks after the addition. Unknown is not the same as zero. Official reference value 30 days from 40 CFR 84.106(d) (EPA AIM Act ER&R rule), effective 2026-01-01. Omit to use it; enter your own figure to override. The result notes say which was used.

startDay.description: Day number of the addition before the first log row (day). Use any day count you like (for example day 0 = 1 January); the rows use the same count. Used only when mode is log; ignored otherwise.

thrComfort.description: Leak rate threshold, comfort cooling. Percent number: 6.2 means 6.2%. Use matching records or an explicitly identified assumption for leak rate threshold, comfort cooling. Unknown is not the same as zero. Official reference value 10% from 40 CFR 84.106(c)(2)(iii) (EPA AIM Act ER&R rule), effective 2026-01-01. Omit to use it; enter your own figure to override. The result notes say which was used. Used only when appliance is comfort; ignored otherwise.

thrCommercial.description: Leak rate threshold, commercial refrigeration. Percent number: 6.2 means 6.2%. Use matching records or an explicitly identified assumption for leak rate threshold, commercial refrigeration. Unknown is not the same as zero. Official reference value 20% from 40 CFR 84.106(c)(2)(i) (EPA AIM Act ER&R rule), effective 2026-01-01. Omit to use it; enter your own figure to override. The result notes say which was used. Used only when appliance is commercial; ignored otherwise.

thrIpr.description: Leak rate threshold, industrial process refrigeration. Percent number: 6.2 means 6.2%. Use matching records or an explicitly identified assumption for leak rate threshold, industrial process refrigeration. Unknown is not the same as zero. Official reference value 30% from 40 CFR 84.106(c)(2)(ii) (EPA AIM Act ER&R rule), effective 2026-01-01. Omit to use it; enter your own figure to override. The result notes say which was used. Used only when appliance is ipr; ignored otherwise.

thrOther.description: Leak rate threshold, refrigerated transport and other appliances. Percent number: 6.2 means 6.2%. Use matching records or an explicitly identified assumption for leak rate threshold, refrigerated transport and other appliances. Unknown is not the same as zero. Official reference value 10% from 40 CFR 84.106(c)(2)(iii) (EPA AIM Act ER&R rule), effective 2026-01-01. Omit to use it; enter your own figure to override. The result notes say which was used. Used only when appliance is other; ignored otherwise.

modelVersion.description: Optional expected method version; a mismatch is rejected.

checkURL.description: Link that replays this calculation on https://buscalc.com/sumtru/verify/. Null when the inputs hold free-form text or the link would be too long.

notes.description: Reference-value notes first, then model notes and the standard limit statement.

referenceValues.description: One entry per official reference value in play: the official figure, the figure used, status official or user, source, effective date and the note text.

sealURL.description: Where a saved record of this result can be sealed with an independent timestamp.
